findings.title: Exclude retrieval-only timestamps from publication fingerprints
findings.description: Supplemental FSC rows get a new projectionCapturedAt on every fetch. Both content_fingerprint and content_hash retain that field, so identical provider values and source bytes become new captures and trigger changed=true on every successful refresh. This contradicts the stated idempotence contract and causes unnecessary archive growth and automated releases.
findings.reproduction: Deep-copy data/dfs-weekly.json; change only every existing row.projectionCapturedAt to a later retrieval time. Compare content_fingerprint for the two snapshots and content_hash for the default slate. Archive the original then the changed copy into a temporary SQLite path.
findings.expected: Identical prices, projections, identities and source content should yield equal semantic fingerprints and insert zero captures when only retrieval time changes. Preserve the timestamp in provenance without treating it as changed provider content.
findings.resolution: Fixed by parent; independently verified against current working-tree corrections.

findings.title: Make reader-visible archive and JSON publication one successful generation
findings.description: The refresh publishes the updated archive before writing the JSON snapshot. If atomic_write fails, the importer throws and reports lastGoodPreserved:true, but the archive has already changed. getDfsSlate overlays archived slates on JSON and exact-week lookups select the latest archive capture, so the failed refresh is immediately reader-visible despite the old JSON remaining intact.
findings.reproduction: Copy shipped JSON and archive to a TemporaryDirectory. Mock fetch/parsers to return the same validated slates with Gibbs projection changed from 23.1 to 23.2. Patch atomic_write to raise OSError('simulated JSON replace failure') and invoke refresh against temporary paths. Read both outputs and the latest archive capture afterward.
findings.expected: On any publication failure, all reader-visible current and exact-week defaults remain at the prior successfully committed generation. A published-generation pointer or coordinated staging/rollback must govern both outputs; simply reversing write order leaves the symmetric failure possible.
findings.resolution: Fixed by parent; independently verified against current working-tree corrections.

findings.title: Track the active capture separately from immutable content identity
findings.description: A -> B -> A source-content recovery skips reusing A as active because the archive deduplicates against any historical equivalent capture. Readers still choose B by captured_at. A transient supplemental outage can therefore keep overriding recovered JSON projections with nulls.
findings.reproduction: Archive shipped default slate A in a temporary database; append B with later capturedAt and all FSC projections unavailable; append recovered original A with a still later capture time, changing only retrieval timestamps.
findings.expected: Recovered A is the default active capture while both immutable captures and their original timestamps remain reproducible.
findings.resolution: Fixed by parent; independently verified against current working-tree corrections.

checks.name: Retrieval-only idempotence
checks.evidence: Final head-enabled implementation: semantic migration inserts 0; new retrieval-only times leave both hashes equal, insert 0, change 0 heads and preserve all archive bytes.

checks.name: Cross-output publication failure
checks.evidence: Final head-enabled implementation: independently injected JSON staging, JSON publication, and archive publication failures each preserve both JSON and archive bytes. Isolated release checkout bounds intermediate-reader exposure.

checks.name: Return to previously archived source content
checks.evidence: Independent A -> B -> A reproduction loaded the actual dfs-store module against temporary data. Current and exact-week APIs restore Wentz 14.95 using original A capture ID/time; head observed time advances; no captures are added; capture rows remain byte-for-value unchanged; explicit B capture still returns null; repeated recovered input is byte-idempotent.
